public_rationale: On February 27, 2026, OpenAI announced a $100 billion expansion over eight years to its existing $38 billion AWS agreement [e1]. The announcement does not isolate payments required for July 2026 through December 2027 [e1]. It also does not establish sufficient delivered capacity across Google, Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle [e1]. This evidence cannot settle the $147 billion threshold or satisfy the early-resolution rule [e1].
limitations: The packet does not establish whether the capacity condition has been met.
No complete payment schedule isolates qualifying obligations for July 2026 through December 2027.
The underlying analyst estimates and their fiscal-to-calendar reconciliation are unavailable.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If hyperscalers build enough capacity, OpenAI needs over $147 billion for compute commitments through end of 2027.

statement.excerpt: Now, all of this is contingent on Google, Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle building enough capacity to capture that revenue, but if we assume that happens, OpenAI needs more than $147 billion just to handle its expected compute commitments through the end of 2027.

from_speaker: contingent on Google, Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle building enough capacity
our_interpretation: The threshold concerns cumulative payments required for compute from the four named providers, not OpenAI's total operating spending.
The surrounding year-and-a-half calculation is read as July 2026 through December 2027. The forecast horizon itself begins on the post date.
Payments for separately excluded providers and activities are not added to the threshold.
The capacity condition requires delivery sufficient to trigger the assumed payment obligations; announced construction plans do not establish it.
criteria.support_condition: The capacity condition is established and qualifying contractual payments required for the assessment period exceed USD 147 billion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The capacity condition is established and a complete, consistently dated accounting of qualifying payment obligations totals USD 147 billion or less.

evidence.explanation: The disclosure establishes a large AWS agreement, but its eight-year scope differs from the forecast's payment window. It cannot establish either the USD 147 billion total or the capacity condition.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Evidence establishing sufficient delivered capacity, together with binding payment schedules or reconciled payments for the four named providers. The records must establish whether required payments for July 2026 through December 2027 exceed $147 billion, without double counting or including amounts outside that period.
